head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: Shaka now preserves HTTP status internally when an empty check lookup fails, but the intended command users still receive generic diagnostics. The implementation stays within scope; verification establishes internal behavior rather than the promised visible outcome.
reasons: The change distinguishes gh failures from malformed JSON and reuses existing error handling without dependencies or configuration.
The pinned commit changes only the planned implementation and test files. One reported review round provides no evidence of approach-level churn; incident frequency and time saved remain unknown.
Reported reproduction, 3454 passing tests, and a live missing-PR lookup support the narrow internal behavior. They do not establish the promised diagnostic for agents and maintainers.
The change affects error reporting without adding persistent effects. Reverting restores the previous diagnostics.
concerns: skills/shaka/lib/shaka/status.rb retains only the generic required-check error message and discards http_status. Consequently, pr and handoff still cannot distinguish rate limiting from other unavailable evidence; pr_watch.rb also re-raises that generic message.

The new checks error message reports only exit 1, not rate limiting or HTTP 403. Tests assert status on the exception object; the packet reports no command-level rate-limit verification. Live rate limiting and GraphQL errors without an HTTP marker remain unexercised.
alternative: Keep this bounded approach and expose the sanitized HTTP status through the existing user-facing diagnostics. Preserve stderr exclusion and unavailable-check blocking. No change would retain the misleading JSON error.
next_action: Revise this PR to carry sanitized HTTP status into check-evidence output and add one command-level rate-limit regression demonstrating what users receive.
